status_reasoning: Reviewers acknowledge that 'Lsd1 has already been shown to be required for hematopoiesis (Sprussel et al, Leukemia 2012)' and state the manuscript is 'technically well done' with favorable evaluation. The claims about Lsd1's requirement for hematopoietic differentiation and resulting pancytopenia are accepted without challenge.

Reviewers note 'A strength of the manuscript is that it integrates CHIP-seq data with gene expression profiling' and find 'The observation that Lsd1 activity is required to repress genes expressed by primitive cells...is conceptually interesting.' The integrative genomic findings showing Lsd1 repression of HSPC genes are accepted.

Reviewers acknowledge the enhancer findings but note 'there was previously published evidence of activity at enhancer elements (Whyte et al. Nature, 2012; Cai et al. Cancer Cell 2011)' and request the authors 'comment on possible other Lsd1-mediated mechanisms' beyond enhancer effects. This suggests the enhancer mechanism alone may not fully explain the phenotypes.

Reviewers state 'The text suggests that Lsd1 deficiency profoundly reduces HSC frequency and function, though this is not apparent when the authors gate on definitive markers in Figure 2' and request 'a bar graph...indicating HSC frequency.' This indicates uncertainty about the magnitude of HSC defects.

Reviewers ask 'Do the authors observe any global changes in H3K4me2/me1 levels that correlate with the reduction in Lsd1 levels?' This question indicates the reviewers want clarification on whether the observed histone methylation changes are global or locus-specific, suggesting uncertainty about the scope of the methylation changes.

Reviewers note 'Sprussel et al. (Leukemia 2012) state that Lsd1 deficiency leads to pancytopenia and apoptosis in erythroid cells' and ask 'Do Kerenyi et al. observe increases in cell death or changes in proliferation among LSK cells, erythroid, or myeloid progenitors?' This indicates the reviewers want clarification on the cellular mechanisms underlying the maturation defects.

Reviewers ask 'Is Lsd1 broadly required for the epigenetic regulation of many cells or is it preferentially required to regulate certain kinds of cells (such as primitive cells)?' and request 'some insight into this question would help to indicate whether this study provides insights of general relevance to other systems.' This indicates uncertainty about the generalizability of the findings beyond hematopoiesis.

Reviewers request discussion of 'how the current results impact upon the concept that LSD1 is a promising therapeutic target for hemoglobinopathies' and note 'one would assume that LSD1 inhibition would be highly problematic, unless modest therapeutic inhibition can be achieved without deleterious influences on hematopoiesis.' This indicates uncertainty about the therapeutic implications given the severe phenotypes observed.

Reviewers request the authors 'comment on how other Lsd1-mediated mechanisms of gene expression regulation (changes in DNA methylation, acetylation changes due to disruption of CoREST complex) may also contribute to the phenotypes observed.' This indicates the reviewers believe alternative mechanisms beyond H3K4 demethylation should be considered.
